full-title: Discovering Cambodia: A Journey Rich in Emotions
quote: Heading to Cambodia, a fascinating country that promises beautiful discoveries and rich emotions! Famous for its majestic temples, but also for one of the darkest periods in its history marked by the Khmer Rouge, Cambodia is a country of many facets.
introduction: We take you with us to discover Cambodia. Our itinerary from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh: travel story with photos, tips and tricks.
google-description: Want to discover Cambodia? From the majestic temples of Angkor Wat to the iconic landscapes of floating villages on Tonle Sap Lake. Between cultural heritage, nature and relaxation, Cambodia has something to charm all travelers. Come with us for a little discovery of Cambodia. Our travelogue with photos, tips and advice.
social-network-description: Cambodia is a country full of surprises. Between the discovery of the impressive ruins of Angkor Wat, the visit to the genocide museum in Phnom Penh and a cruise on the Mekong to discover floating villages, Cambodia offers a great diversity of experiences and discoveries.

what-time-of-year.title: When to go?
what-time-of-year.part1: #November to March#, dry season, is noted as the best season with more pleasant temperatures, very little rain and low humidity. However, lots of people.
what-time-of-year.part2: #April to October#, during the rainy season, called the monsoon, it is much heavier and there is also more humidity, which can quickly become exhausting.
what-time-of-year.part3: We therefore consider that Cambodia has two distinct seasons. However, temperatures vary very little throughout the year and are always between 25 and 30 °C depending on humidity.
what-time-of-year.part4: On our side, we went in April, a mix between the two, not too much humidity yet, very hot though and crowds but not packed either. Not a single day of rain during our stay, maybe a bit of luck with us.

how-long.title: How long?
how-long.part1: If you plan to have a few days of rest between each visit, and you do roughly the same route as us, we recommend coming for 7 days.
how-long.part2: Devote #three days to Siem Reap# to explore [the temples of the Angkor site](angkor-wat), but also Lake Tonle Sap and enjoy the city's atmosphere. Then continue with #two days in Phnom Penh# to visit the Royal Palace, [the Tuol Sleng museum](tuol-sleng-genocide-museum), the Choeung Ek memorial site (Killing Fields) and stroll around the city.
how-long.part3: Between transport, the activity itself and unforeseen events, it is better to leave plenty of room in your schedule. And maybe you want to relax a little too, after all these are holidays!

how-much.title: How much money to budget?
how-much.part1: Cambodia attracts travelers because it's a country that offers the possibility to travel without breaking the bank. This destination offers options adapted to different budgets.
how-much.part2: #For a budget stay, plan around 50 € per day and per person#. Hotels are not very expensive and you can find them even with a small budget. Street food is on every corner and you will always find something to snack on. As for transport, the tuk-tuk remains a must.
how-much.part3: With a budget of around 100 € per day and per person, you can enjoy a better level of comfort, staying in a certainly more pleasant hotel, but above all by participating in some excursions or guided activities.
how-much.part4: Note, we are talking about our own experience and it may be that year after year and with growing tourism, prices increase a little.

moving-around.title: How to get around locally?
moving-around.part1: Traveling in Cambodia is relatively simple thanks to the different means of transport adapted to all budgets.
moving-around.part2: #Tuk-tuks# are very present in Cambodian cities. Practical and cheap, they allow you to move easily over short distances and reach the main tourist sites of each city.
moving-around.part3: To travel from one city to another, several options are possible: #bus, minibus or private taxi#. The bus remains the most practical and economical way to reach the main destinations of the country.
moving-around.part4: Download #Grab# to avoid any price scams and be able to book your trips safely.
moving-around.part5: Even if distances seem short on the map, journeys can be quite long in Cambodia. Better to plan enough time between each stage, especially because of traffic and road conditions.
moving-around.part6: You will also find #Sleeper buses#: night buses connecting major cities where you have individual or double bunks, in ours there were only doubles it seems. Much less comfortable than a real hotel bed, but it allows you to save a hotel night while covering long distances.
moving-around.part7: This is what we took with [Giant Ibis](https://www.giantibis.com/) during our stay to go from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh at night, between 6 and 8 hours on the road depending on traffic and road conditions.

where-to-stay.title: Where to sleep?
where-to-stay.part1: In Cambodia, accommodation options are numerous and adapted to all budgets. Whether you are looking for a simple dormitory, a private room or a more comfortable hotel, you will easily find an option that suits you.
where-to-stay.part2: In Phnom Penh, Siem Reap and the main tourist destinations, #youth hostels, guesthouses and hotels# are very present. For those who want more comfort, the country also offers beautiful high-end establishments and luxury hotels.

what-to-bring.title: What to pack?
what-to-bring.part1: Remember to pack #light and comfortable clothing#, adapted to the heat. Also plan a few outfits covering arms and legs for visiting temples, but also to protect yourself from mosquitoes.
what-to-bring.part2: Don't forget your #raincoat or poncho#, as showers are frequent.
what-to-bring.part3: For shoes, take your daily shoes. Add a pair of #hiking shoes# or trekking shoes for excursions and temple visits.
what-to-bring.part5: A small first aid kit with basic medications, especially for digestive issues, as well as bandages.
what-to-bring.part7: Sunscreen with a high protection factor.
what-to-bring.part8: A hat or cap to protect you from the sun.
what-to-bring.part10: A water bottle to stay well hydrated throughout the day.
what-to-bring.part12: Always keep photocopies of all your important documents with you.
what-to-bring.part13: To learn more, feel free to read our article on how to prepare your trip to Cambodia, where we explain in detail everything you need to travel safely.

itinerary.title: Our itinerary
itinerary.part1: Cambodia is a Southeast Asian country. It is bordered by Thailand, Laos and Vietnam.
itinerary.part3: By the way, I remind you here, but when we suggest a number of visit days, this obviously doesn't count the time difference, if you have one and need a little adaptation time, as well as the flight travel time.
itinerary.part4: For the record, we live in [Singapore](singapore) and traveling in Asia is very simple for us. Reaching Cambodia for example only took us 2h, inevitably much less than if you come from [France](france) for example.

visit.title: SIEM REAP
visit.part1: True starting point to explore the temples of Angkor, Siem Reap is one of the must-visit destinations during a stay in Cambodia.
visit.part2: If the temples will certainly be at the heart of your visit, also take the time to #discover the city of Siem Reap#. Between its markets, its small streets, its restaurants and its pleasant atmosphere, the city deserves to be lingered in, despite its tourist crowds.
visit.part3: On our side and like certainly most travelers, we mostly enjoyed Siem Reap in the evening, between its night markets and its main street.

visit1.title: #✓ Pub Street#
visit1.part1: At nightfall, Siem Reap shows you a new facet, that of a #modern, dynamic and festive city#.
visit1.part2: Pub Street is one of the most lively places. Its many bars and cafes attract visitors from all over the world to extend the evening. Musicians, DJs and dancers animate the streets. You will also find quite a few shops and small markets still open.
visit1.part3: For gastronomy, you won't be left out with street stalls and restaurants offering Cambodian specialties and world cuisines. The most curious can even try fried insects, a local unusual specialty.
visit1.part4: If you want to taste Cambodian specialties, we strongly recommend 3 dishes: Amok Trei, Lok Lak and Khmer Red Curry.
visit1.part5: The [Khmer Red Curry](khmer-red-curry): Much less spicy than curries from other Asian countries we know such as [Thailand](thailand) for example, Khmer red curry is a kind of stew simmered in coconut milk with melting meat and vegetables, not forgetting the red curry paste.
visit1.part6: The [Lok Lak](lok-lak): Beef marinated in a mixture of soy sauce, nuoc nam sauce and especially Kampot pepper then seared in a wok and accompanied by rice and a salad. A dish both salty, slightly sweet and fragrant.
visit1.part7: The [Amok Trei](amok-trei): Dish mainly based on fish, elevated by a creamy coconut cream, Khmer curry and lemongrass. A recipe traditionally steamed in a banana leaf.
visit1.part8: Another unusual experience: #fish spa#, or pedicure with small fish, which consists of dipping your feet in a basin where small fish remove dead skin. You will find them at almost every street corner.
visit1.part9: But as we said above, Siem Reap is especially known for being the gateway to the famous archaeological site of Angkor.

visit2.title: ANGKOR TEMPLES
visit2.part1: True emblem of the country, this vast ensemble of temples attracts visitors from all over the world every year.
visit2.part2: #Angkor Wat#, its most famous monument, is today a #true national symbol# and is known and recognized worldwide. It is indeed the image we use when we want to talk about or illustrate [Cambodia](cambodia).
visit2.part3: Among the emblematic monuments of the complex, #Angkor Thom# is the entrance gate to the splendid #Bayon temple#, famous for its gigantic towers adorned with smiling faces, also known as the temple of 1000 faces.
visit2.part4: If you wish to walk in Lara Croft's footsteps, the #Ta Prohm temple# stands out thanks to its imposing trees whose roots gradually reclaim the space and invade the remains. Over 600 years old, its trees envelop the site with a mysterious and timeless aura.
visit2.part5: A little less known, #the water temple Neak Poan# is part of the slightly more relaxing visits, less invaded by the noise of tuk tuk horns and tourists. It is accessed by a long wooden walkway above a lake with lotus flowers.
visit2.part6: If like us you stay 3 days to visit the temples, you will be able to discover many more. From the lesser known to the most remote, from the best preserved to the most buried in the jungle.
visit2.part7: With their superbly detailed sculptures, the temples tell a fascinating story.
visit2.part8: #Its impressive architecture makes it a unique place#.
visit2.part9: Also enjoy your stay in Siem Reap to take a boat excursion on Tonle Sap, the largest lake in Cambodia.

visit3.title: TONLE SAP LAKE
visit3.part1: Tonle Sap refers to both #the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia#, as well as the river connecting the lake to the Mekong.
visit3.part2: It has a unique hydrological functioning in the world.
visit3.part3: Every year, during the monsoon, between July and October, #the lake's surface area is multiplied by 4# due to the Mekong floods reversing the river's current.
visit3.part4: This spectacular natural phenomenon therefore causes a sharp rise in water levels which creates another peculiarity of the lake:
visit3.part5: Houses, shops and schools have settled on the water and adapt to the lake's level variations, #houses built on stilts#, several meters high forming villages nicknamed floating villages.
visit3.part6: A landscape as surprising as it is unusual. A bit like [the Can Tho floating market](can-tho) in [Vietnam](vietnam).
visit3.part7: There are several villages open to tourism: Me Chreay, Chong Kneas, Kampong Phluk, Kampong Luong and Kampong Khleang.
visit3.part8: For our trip to Cambodia, we visited #Kampong Phluk village#.
visit3.part9: The road to get there is deserted. We glimpse a few small food stalls on the side of the path, but not a single car on the horizon. The journey is quite chaotic: it's far from a classic road, it's more of a red sand path.
visit3.part10: Finally, when we say there was no one on the road, it's not entirely true! Keep an eye out, as little creatures can appear and cross without warning!
visit3.part11: After traveling this long dirt road, we finally arrive at our destination and discover these houses on stilts. A landscape as surprising as it is fascinating, a testament to the remarkable adaptability of its inhabitants to their environment.
visit3.part12: After our discovery of Siem Reap and its surroundings, let's head together to discover this other must-see city in Cambodia.

visit4.title: PHNOM PENH
visit4.part1: #Capital of Cambodia#, Phnom Penh marked its history with the dark years of the Khmer Rouge regime, until 1979. Since then, the city has been able to revive and transform itself to become a dynamic and modern destination.
visit4.part2: Between its temples, its historical heritage, its lively markets and its nightlife, Phnom Penh offers a beautiful diversity of things to do, adapted to all traveler profiles.

visit5.title: #✓ Royal Palace#
visit5.part1: True emblem of [Phnom Penh](phnom-penh), the Royal Palace is a must-visit during your stay.
visit5.part2: Official residence of the king and the Cambodian royal family, it impresses with its traditional Khmer architecture, #its golden roofs and its elegant white enclosure#.
visit5.part3: This magnificent ensemble houses several pavilions, including the famous #Silver Pagoda#, recognizable by its floor covered with silver tiles and its precious Buddhas, as well as superb gardens.
visit5.part4: A visit that allows you to #discover all the richness of Cambodia's heritage and traditions#.
visit5.part5: If you have the opportunity, come early in the morning. The sun rising and reflecting on the walls and the gold color of the palace is superb.

visit6.title: #✓ National Museum of Cambodia#
visit6.part1: Located near the Royal Palace, the National Museum is also a must-visit.
visit6.part2: We discover notably sculptures, religious and cultural objects, ceramics.
visit6.part3: This visit allows us to better understand the history and way of life of the Khmers at that time.
visit6.part4: The museum also deserves the detour for its architecture, #recognizable by its elegant red tile roofs# and its interior courtyard, which gives it a very particular charm.
visit6.part5: Since photos are forbidden inside, we'll let you discover it for yourself, or admire the beauty of the exterior.

visit7.title: #✓ Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum#
visit7.part1: The Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum, formerly known as #S-21 prison#, is installed in a former high school transformed into a detention and torture center. Thousands of people were #imprisoned, tortured and executed# under the regime of Pol Pot, leader of the Khmer Rouge.
visit7.part2: Today become a museum, #the site pays tribute to the victims# and allows visitors to better understand this particularly dark period of Cambodia's history.
visit7.part3: The visit allows visitors to become aware of the magnitude of the tragedy experienced by the Cambodian population. We can discover the former cells, photographs of prisoners, as well as numerous documents and testimonies that tell their story.
visit7.part4: Just like [the War Remnants Museum](ho-chi-minh-war-museum) in [Vietnam](vietnam), this type of visit is strong in emotion. Designated as dark tourism by some people, I rather want to say for me that it's #memory tourism#, to remember and understand the country's history.

bonus.title: Bonus
bonus.part1: Still too wild during our first visit to Cambodia, Mondulkiri, region located in the East of Cambodia, is opening up more and more to travelers in search of nature and authenticity.
bonus.part2: This region offers you magnificent landscapes for the moment still far from the bustle of the most visited places in Cambodia. Between treks in the jungle, discovery of waterfalls, exchanges with local communities and encounters with elephants, Mondulkiri allows you to discover another face of Cambodia.
bonus.part3: Here is the end of our little visit to Cambodia.
bonus.part4: See you every Saturday for a detailed article on each of our visits.

conclusion: Cambodia surprises with its contrasts: temples imbued with serenity, a moving history and inhabitants whose smiles and kindness mark travelers.
